# E0210: primitive type name used as a name

Type names such as `str`, `i64` and `bool` can't name anything else. Choose another name, such as `text`.

- Rule: [`lexical.primitive-type-names`](../../reference/02-lexical.md#lexical.primitive-type-names)
- Reported at: the name.
- Tier: `core`, checked in the `types` phase

## Example

This program makes the mistake:

```stilt E0210:2
fn label() -> str {
  let str = "a"
  str
}
```

This one is fixed:

```stilt
fn label() -> str {
  let text = "a"
  text
}
```

## What the compiler prints

`stilt check` on [`E0210_primitive_type_name_used_as_a_name.lt`](../../tests/diagnostics/E0210_primitive_type_name_used_as_a_name.lt):

```text
── PRIMITIVE TYPE NAME USED AS A NAME ── E0210_primitive_type_name_used_as_a_name.lt:2:7  [E0210]

`str` is a primitive type name:

  2 │   let str = "a"
    │       ^^^

Type names such as `str`, `i64` and `bool` can't name anything else. Choose
another name, such as `text`.
```
